prompt: Write the body (about 150 words) of an insurer's answer to a personal injury petition in Texas: a general denial and three affirmative defenses that fit a rear-end collision. Plain text. Call the parties only 'Plaintiff' and 'Defendant'. No names, placeholders, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1097; do not mention it.)
text:
Defendant generally denies each and every allegation contained in Plaintiff's Original Petition and demands strict proof thereof by a preponderance of the evidence, as required by the Texas Rules of Civil Procedure.

Subject to and without waiving the foregoing general denial, Defendant asserts the following affirmative defenses.

First, Plaintiff's alleged injuries and damages were not proximately caused by any negligent act or omission of Defendant. The collision at issue was caused, in whole or in part, by the acts or omissions of Plaintiff, including following too closely and failing to keep a proper lookout.

Second, Plaintiff failed to mitigate damages by unreasonably delaying or declining recommended medical treatment, and any recovery must be reduced accordingly.

Third, under Chapter 33 of the Texas Civil Practice and Remedies Code, Defendant requests that the trier of fact determine the percentage of responsibility attributable to Plaintiff and any other responsible third party, and that any recovery be reduced or barred in accordance with the proportionate responsibility statute.

Defendant reserves the right to amend this Answer as discovery proceeds.
